issues.description: Method getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor(): the problem statement's UML (problem_statement.md) declares getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor() with return type double, but the reference solution (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) declares the method as returning int. This is a real contradiction: the UML indicates a fractional (double) result is expected (students per tutor may be non-integer), while the solution uses integer division and returns an int, losing fractional information and creating confusion about the expected return type and implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix: change the solution method signature to return double and perform floating-point division, for example: public double getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor() { return (double) getTotalNumberOfStudents() / getNumberOfTutors(); } Also update the template TODO/comments to indicate a double return type if needed. Alternatively, if integer division is intended, update the problem statement UML to show an int return type and document that the value is rounded/truncated.
